notes: Check batch: four runs (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), no Opus, so per_rule marks opus unavailable. All four ran with rc 0, read SKILL.md only (Expected reads met) and saw the reworded `with` text in the transcript. In the scratch folder, with a local Decimal build on the code path, all four pass mix format --check-formatted, compile without warnings and pass their one doctest; a probe confirmed haiku-1 raises on bad input (MatchError for amount "abc", FunctionClauseError for status "shipped") while the other three return {:error, reason}.

Changed rule, now in the case's list and graded per run: "Chain fallible steps with `with`; normalize each step's error in a small private function". The one-step verdict is decided by "A `with` has at least two `<-` steps; one step is a `case`." and "When the body of a one-step `with` calls another function that can fail, that call is the second step: chain it with a second `<-` instead of nesting a `case` or adding an `else`." (idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md, that rule's first paragraph and its paragraph after the first example). Violating runs out of 4: one-step `with` 2 (sonnet-1 line 66, sonnet-2 line 74, each wrapping parse_orders/1 in build/1; the body calls nothing that can fail); `else` 0 (no run wrote an else). No run nests a case in a with: haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 chain string_field/2 and parse_amount/1 as two steps (haiku-2 lines 109-110, sonnet-1 lines 88-89, sonnet-2 lines 95-96). Haiku-1 writes no with (not exercised); haiku-2 handles its single call with case (line 53).

Comparison for the `with` rule: the first check batch had one-step 2 of 4 (both Sonnet runs, four one-step withs each, three of them nesting a case) and else 0 of 4; here the Sonnet runs keep only the one-step with in build/1. The previous sweep recorded only skill-sonnet-1's else (lines 111-112), 1 of 4 Haiku and Sonnet runs, and flagged no one-step with, though a re-read shows the shape in all four of its Haiku and Sonnet skill runs (haiku-1 line 55, haiku-2 line 56, sonnet-1 line 63, sonnet-2 lines 65, 110, 119 and 128), so its free-text count of 0 for that sentence understates it.

Changed rule, graded against the current text as in the first check batch: "Use the `Enum` or `Map` function made for the job", decided by its second table row: "a `reduce` that reads and writes one key per element is these two written by hand". Hand-written per-key fold: 0 of 4. All four group with Enum.group_by/2 and summarize with Map.new/2 or, in haiku-2, Enum.map/2 into a sorted list; haiku-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 count completed orders with Enum.frequencies_by/2, haiku-2 with Enum.count/1 on each customer's filtered orders. The Decimal sums (haiku-1 line 97, haiku-2 line 95, sonnet-1 line 155, sonnet-2 line 157) are reductions no table row replaces, as before. Same count as the first check batch (0 of 4).

Changed rule, graded against the current text as in the first check batch: Naming (fetch sentence: "A function that looks a key up and also checks the value, returning `{:error, reason}`, is not a `fetch`: name it by its job, such as `string_field/2` or `parse_amount/1`."; variable sentence: "A variable may carry the name of the external key it holds, as in `%{"data" => data}`, since the payload chose that name."). Violating runs per sentence, out of 4: modules CamelCase and snake_case 0; top-level namespace 0 (Reports.Orders as the prompt names it, Order nested under it); boolean functions end in ? 0 (no run defines one, not exercised); get/fetch 0 (haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 name the lookup-and-check helper string_field/2; haiku-1 has none); size/length 0 (not exercised); ignored values 0; domain variable names 0 (no data, item, res or x; text and value held to the earlier standard, which passed text, parsed and value and flagged only data and single letters).

Unchanged rule, new finding: "Use captures for one-call lambdas and `fn` for anything longer" is decided by "When the body does more than one call or would need `&2`, write `fn` with named arguments." Sonnet-1 (line 155: &Decimal.add(&2, &1.amount)) and sonnet-2 (line 157: &Decimal.add(&1.amount, &2)) use &2 in a capture, so 2 of 4 runs violate it. Neither the previous sweep nor the first check batch wrote a &2 capture in this case, so Sonnet moving from clean to violated reflects what these runs wrote, not a change in standard. Both haiku runs sum with &Decimal.add/2.

Other unchanged rules follow the earlier standard: Decimal.parse/1 catch-alls go under Match every expected shape (haiku-2 line 138, sonnet-1 line 117, sonnet-2 line 124); haiku-1's raising on malformed rows and its key match with no no-match clause are listed as in the first check batch's haiku-1, and its Order struct without @type t is listed under the struct rule (earlier structs in this case all had one); its two-step pipeline on one line is listed as in the previous sweep's skill-haiku-1; reduce_while piped into case or then/2 is not listed, as in the first check batch's Sonnet runs. The three catch-alls repeat verbatim the line `_other -> {:error, {:invalid_field, "amount"}}` from the skill's own one-step `with` example (idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md line 165, the "Instead of" side), moved into parse_amount/1 as the "write" side suggests, so that example models a catch-all another rule flags.
